input.question: Why am I more tired on some mornings than others even if I get around the same sleep every night?
input.ground_truth: It's all about your sleep cycle. You can be sleeping nearly the same amount every night but waking up during different phases of sleep can effect your sleepiness level. There are clocks designed to wake you up at the perfect point in your sleep cycle. Now this may mean that you wake up a little earlier or later than you intended to but you will feel more rested if you wake at the right point in your sleep cycle.

Okay! Let’s imagine your body is like a toy car and sleep is like the battery that makes it run.

Sometimes, even if you charge your toy car (sleep in your bed) for the same amount of time every night, it might not run as well the next day. Maybe yesterday you played a lot outside (that’s like being active or thinking a lot), or maybe you felt worried or excited (that’s like your brain working extra hard). All those things can make your battery (your body) use up more energy, so you feel more tired in the morning.

Also, sometimes your body just needs a little more rest, even if you slept the same number of hours. It’s like how sometimes you need an extra snack even if you ate breakfast and lunch.

So, even with the same amount of sleep, your body might feel more tired some mornings because of what you did the day before or how your body feels inside.
